newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG's Orogen sees Moran oil output in Oct.
newsitem.headline: PNG's Orogen sees Moran oil output in Oct.

text.p: Papua New Guinea resources group Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it expected the Moran oil field in PNG to be producing 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil by October this year or shortly after under an extended well test arrangement.
Orogen managing director Charles Lepani said he expected production to rise to 30,000 bpd by the middle-to-end of next year, and to exceed 100,000 bpd in around two years.
Director Kevin McCann told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing that drilling earlier this year had revealed a vertical oil column of 1,100 metres.
Partners in the field have not given any estimate of reserves, although joint venturer Oil Search Ltd has said the Moran-2X sidetrack well intersected a vertical oil column of 800 metres.
"We had an unhappy experience with Gobe where it took five or ten years to actually get on to this," Lepani told reporters.

"Now we are combining the process of getting the memorandum of understanding with landowners and getting government approvals going so we compress the period to three-plus, rather than a five-ten year period," he said.
Funds from early production would assist in the development of the project, he added.
Lepani said it was hoped to begin production at 10,000 barrels a day in October, although some landowner issues still needed to be resolved.
Orogen has a 15.75 percent stake in licence PDL-2, which is operated by Chevron Corp unit Chevron Niugini with 19.375 percent.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd has 9.688 percent, Mobil Corp 11.612 percent, BP Australia Ltd 19.375 pecent, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd affiliate Japan Papua New Guinea Petroleum Co Ltd (JPP) 4.844 percent, Merlin Pacific Oil Co NL 4.844 percent, Oil Search 7.763 percent, and Petroleum Resources Kutubu Pty Ltd 6.75 percent.
